name: leads-out-of-area
about: Earlier ads drew many leads from too far away; the plan should say where the job is.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days, 40 were called and 27 were reached.
19 of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days were closed as: out of area.
4 of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days were closed as: not interested.

output.audience: Class A flatbed drivers who meet the experience requirement and live where the Midwest lanes run. They likely drive for a larger fleet now, out longer or in a shared truck. The pay per mile, home weekly and an assigned truck, with the area named plainly, would make them stop.

angles.idea: State plainly who this is for: Class A flatbed drivers on Midwest lanes who meet the experience requirement.
angles.proof: The job is regional, on Midwest lanes, and states an experience requirement.
angles.why: A large share of recent leads were closed as out of area. Stating the lanes and the requirement up front filters before the form. No hook or scene has been measured yet.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile for regional flatbed work, and name the Midwest lanes beside it.
angles.proof: The opening states a pay per mile, on flatbed, on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Pay is the fact a working driver compares fastest. Naming the lanes next to it helps keep out-of-area drivers from applying. Untested for this carrier.

angles.idea: Lead with being home weekly, shown as a driver's truck-free day on a Midwest home street.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Home time is the job's clearest life fact and fits regional drivers. Nothing has been measured for this hook, so it is a starting bet.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck: the same flatbed rig waiting for the same driver, parked and ready.
angles.proof: The job lists an assigned truck and flatbed work.
angles.why: Flatbed drivers care about their equipment, and showing flatbed screens out drivers who do not want that work. There is no earlier result to lean on.

angles.idea: Lead with the small fleet where dispatch knows the driver's name, seen from the driver's seat.
angles.proof: The carrier describes itself as a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.why: This is the carrier's own line and sets it apart from large fleets. Some recent leads closed as not interested, so a clearer picture of the job may help. Unmeasured.
